chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from a number of our companions, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Delay [the upbringing/discipline of] your child until he reaches six years, then bring him close to you for seven years, and discipline him with your discipline; if he accepts and is good, [well and good], otherwise let him be."

key_terms.أَدَبِكَ: Your discipline / your manner of upbringing
key_terms.ضُمَّهُ إِلَيْكَ: Bring him close to you / attach him to you
key_terms.فَخَلِّ عَنْهُ: Then let him go / leave him alone

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic approach to disciplining children at different ages?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on developmental psychology in upbringing, distinguishing between early childhood (0-6), formative mentorship (6-13), and the transition to autonomy. The phrase 'if he accepts and is sound, otherwise leave him' highlights the principle of *adab* (discipline/character formation) through gentle guidance rather than coercion, a key tenet in Al-Kulayni’s and Al-Tusi’s legal discussions on parental rights. It underscores the balance between authority and the child’s emerging agency, a theme central to Shia family jurisprudence.
